interpretation: Intervention was effective: original-wrong B roots under Aall+launched nonfinal were corrected and reused. No matching convincing throughput gain.

More B reuse does not imply longer coherent accepted tails: original tails remain generated under the old root. Treatment emitted fewer tokens per verified window and required more stage1 rows/windows in these forced runs, despite fewer launched stage0 rows.
This partial oracle is not an upper bound for a correction/drafter that regenerates a coherent tail under the corrected root. It tests only retaining original tails/confidence/readiness.

Algorithmic intervention per decision leaves widths/gate factors/ready outputs/chain work settings unchanged. Total MTP chain counts/head work change with the new path and are reported, not assumed constant.
